decisions.executionNote: Approach the floral bunny with the left arm, open gripper; small initial increments to preserve elbow configuration and assess tracking.
Replan after continuity rejection with smaller translation; align left gripper toward the bunny torso while lowering gently.
Continue a slow left-arm approach, maintaining open jaws and orientation while moving toward the bunny's centerline.
Raise slightly and tip the left gripper downward while advancing; prior lowering showed tracking residual, so use a higher approach.
Advance the open left gripper above the bunny's front, gradually angling fingers downward toward the upper torso.
Bring the open fingertips closer to the bunny's upper body, using the wrist image for lateral alignment and preserving arm configuration.
Correct the left gripper laterally toward the bunny's torso in the head view and advance slightly; depth is still uncertain.
Close the left gripper around the bunny's upper torso with only a small final forward approach; verify retention visually on a subsequent lift.
Lift the closed left gripper by 4.5 cm as a retention check; look for the bunny moving with the fingers and feet clearing the tabletop.
Retention is not clear and the jaws appear empty. Reopen, lower slightly, and move left/forward to place the bunny deeper between the fingers.
Reposition open fingers lower around the floral-dress torso rather than the face, correcting leftward and advancing cautiously.
Seat the bunny's torso farther inside the open jaws, then close fully while maintaining the current low approach height.
Hold the left hand stationary with fully closed command so the torso grasp can settle before another lift test.
The fingers visually close in front of the doll rather than retaining it. Reopen and advance deeper, keeping the torso centered.
Advance the open fingers farther past the front of the floral dress and slightly lower, aiming to enclose the torso instead of pinching its front surface.
Center the shifted torso between the fingers, lower a little to avoid the head, and close the left gripper for a deeper grasp.
Maintain the fully closed target without translation to finish seating the deeper torso grasp before testing lift.
The torso now appears between separated gripping surfaces. Test retention with a slow 4 cm vertical lift, keeping the left gripper closed.
The bunny slipped out of the frontal grasp. Reopen, raise clear, and rotate toward a downward approach to reduce further pushing.
Replan the rejected clearance motion with smaller upward and pitch increments, keeping the left gripper open.
Continue raising and tilting the open left gripper downward, advancing only slightly to establish an overhead approach.
Continue the downward approach orientation while raising enough to clear the bunny's head; make a small rightward alignment correction.
Align the open jaws around the upper head from above with a steeper approach; compensate forward as the fingertips rotate downward.
Close the downward-angled jaws around the bunny's head with a small lateral correction, avoiding further forward pushing.
Keep the head grasp closed, allow it to settle, then test a small vertical lift while checking that the bunny stays fixed relative to the fingers.
Continue a slow closed-gripper lift to distinguish retention from slipping; the bunny moved during the last test, but its attachment is uncertain.
Retention is still not visible. Reopen and reposition the downward gripper farther over the bunny, lowering the wrist to maintain reach margin.
Avoid extending farther. Lower vertically toward the nearer foot/lower dress visible between the jaws and close for an alternative grasp.
Finish closing around the nearer bunny foot, then begin a tiny upward/retracting retention test to preserve reach margin.
Lift and retract gently with the foot grasp closed; check whether the foot remains between the jaws and the doll clears the table.
The foot now stays between the jaws as the bunny tilts. Continue lifting while retracting to keep the elbow-up arm away from full extension.
Maintain the retained foot grasp and raise another 5 cm while retracting; the hanging body needs additional clearance beyond the foot's lift.
Keep the bunny held by its foot, lift and retract farther, and gently reduce downward pitch to gain clearance without nearing full extension.
